versions.content: Loop-back signal flow in sender-receiver communication Type: valid Description: It shall be possible to annotate connections among SW-Cs on VFB level, to indicate that a sender-receiver communication needs to be buffered. Rationale: When software components are connected to work together using sender-receiver communication there is a natural signal flow implied in this composition where one SW-Component produces some data which is then consumed and further processed by another software component. When such a setup also contains loop-back of signals it is no longer possible to determine which signal-flow is to be processed during one pass and which signal flow shall be buffered as the loop-back for the next execution. Use Case: A filter algorithm which is implemented using several software components and feeds the result of the algorithm back as an input. When this loop-back signal flow is annotated, the relationships between the other software components can be arranged in a sequence and the execution order of the involved runnable entities can be determined. Analysis and validation of timing behavior in closed loop control systems Dependencies: [RS_TIMEX_00001], [RS_TIMEX_00003] Supporting Material: Requirements on BSW & RTE Features

versions.content: Specification of timing resources for software-component description Type: valid Description: The AUTOSAR templates shall provide means to impose execution time constraints on executable entities in order to ensure temporal resource consumption. Rationale: One of the main criteria for mapping of SW-C onto ECUs is the resource requirement of the complete SW system assigned to a single ECU. In order to estimate the total amount of resources required for a software system, it is necessary to have the information for each of the assigned SW-Cs. Concerning this use case, the relevant CPU specific resource information is the worst case execution time. Again, please note that the overall use case can not fully be covered within the scope of this document because the final assessment of resource consumption is only feasible in the context of an ECU configuration. On the other hand, the assessment in the scope of the ECU configuration needs preparation by specifying resource claims in the scope of a software-component. This constraint is mainly caused by the fact that the relevant basic software configuration can only be available in the scope of an ECU configuration for the first time in the workflow. It is obvious that the basic software contributes to a more or less large extend to the overall resource consumption. Use Case: For integration purposes it is necessary to specify the worst case execution time of an executable entity in order to ensure proper integration with regard to temporal requirements. Dependencies: [FDUC 3.2.8] Supporting Material: None

versions.content: Support for events indicating variable accesses Type: valid Description: The Timing Extension shall provide means to reference the point-in-time when executable entities, namely runnable entities, access variables. Rationale: In some cases it is necessary to reference the point-in-time when executable entities access variable data and being capable to impose timing constraints on these timing description events. But there may be several executable entities accessing such variable data, but some of those executable entities may have different age timing constraints. In order to avoid that such runnable entities are mapped to a task with a higher activation frequency than required, it would be good to annotate the specific variable access. Use Case: None Dependencies: [RS_TIMEX_00001] Supporting Material: None

versions.content: Support for Logical Execution Time Type: valid Description: The AUTOSAR templates shall provide the means to support the description of Logical Execution Time (LET) respectively Time Determinism. In particular the following shall be described: • Parameters of a LET interval : Length, type of recurrence and recurrence • The relation between LET intervals, like offset, gap and overlap. • Executable entities and/or groups of executable entities that shall be executed in the context of LET. • Data exchange that shall be conducted in the context of a LET interval, namely the time deterministic exchange of data between executable entities and/or groups of executable entities. • Means to specify an order of execution among a number of executable entities. Rationale: Time determinism is a crucial characteristic in embedded distributed real-time systems that ensures: • reliable operation of such systems due to deterministic data exchange and execution of executable entities, and • analysis and validation of such systems in order to perform timing analysis early in the development process. Use Case: Design and define timing behavior of applications as well as analysis and validation of timing behavior. Dependencies: [RS_TIMEX_00001], [RS_TIMEX_00002], [RS_TIMEX_00003], [RS_TIMEX_00004], [RS_TIMEX_00006] Supporting Material: None

versions.content: Support for Specifying Synchronization Type: valid Description: The AUTOSAR templates shall provide the means to support specification of synchronization among executable entities and/or groups of executable entities. Rationale: In some cases it is not sufficient to specify the execution order of executable entities and use synchronization timing constraints to express that executable entities must not be executed before others have completed their execution. The Execution Order Constraint provided by the AUTOSAR Timing Extensions allows to specify an order among executable entities but does not provide means to specify where in this order synchronization means shall be used to guarantee that a number of executable entities complete execution before other executable entities are permitted to start execution. The Synchronization Timing Constraint provided by the AUTOSAR Timing Extensions allows specifying synchronization with regard to temporal characteristics, namely a time interval. Use Case: Ensure proper synchronization during execution of executable entities which are executed in different tasks and on different cores. Dependencies: [RS_TIMEX_00022] Supporting Material: None
